query: Do federal judges appointed by different Presidents (Trump vs. other Republican vs. Democratic) differ in their voting tendencies on immigration injunction cases? Do Trump-appointed judges tend to be more supportive of Trump administration immigration policies compared to judges appointed by other Republican or Democratic presidents?

schema.name: judge_name
schema.definition: The full name of the federal judge who authored or signed the decision.
schema.rationale: Required to identify the specific judge and link them to their appointing President.

schema.name: appointing_president
schema.definition: The United States President who appointed the judge to the federal bench.
schema.rationale: Directly addresses the core research question comparing Trump appointees, other Republican appointees, and Democratic appointees.

schema.name: ruling_on_immigration_policy
schema.definition: The judge's ruling or vote on the challenged immigration policy or executive action.
schema.rationale: Measures the judge's voting tendency and supportiveness toward the administration's immigration policies.

schema.name: challenged_policy_type
schema.definition: The specific type of immigration policy or executive action being challenged in the case.
schema.rationale: Allows researchers to control for the specific type of policy (e.g., birthright citizenship, Alien Enemies Act, legal representation programs) when comparing voting patterns.

schema.name: injunction_scope_granted
schema.definition: The geographic or party scope of the preliminary injunction or temporary restraining order granted by the judge.
schema.rationale: Helps analyze whether judges differ in their willingness to issue sweeping nationwide/universal injunctions versus party-specific relief.
